unit.title: Numbers and Sequences
unit.blurb: Counting on and back in steps, including through zero, linear sequences, square and triangular numbers, and prime and composite numbers.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Count on and back in steps of constant size, including through zero, and continue linear sequences.

O2.t: Recognise and use square numbers and triangular numbers.

O3.t: Recognise prime and composite numbers and find factors of numbers up to 100.

p: A **linear sequence** goes up or down by the same amount each time. 50, 42, 34, 26, … counts back in **eights**.
You can count back past zero: 9, 5, 1, −3, −7, …

lesson.t: Why the step works backwards too
p: If a sequence adds the same amount each time, we can subtract that amount to go back, even past zero into negative numbers.

lesson.q: The sequence is 14, 10, 6, … Write the next three terms.

p: Find the step.
Apply it again and again.
Count carefully across 0.
Counting back 4 from 2 gives −2.

p: A **square number** is made by multiplying a number by itself: 4 × 4 = **16**. Dots for a square number make a square.
**Triangular numbers** make a triangle of dots: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, … Each time, add one more than last time: +2, +3, +4, …

lesson.t: Why they are called square and triangular
p: Square numbers make square patterns of dots (n × n). Triangular numbers make triangles: 1, 1 + 2, 1 + 2 + 3, …

steps: add one more row each time

p: Square: multiply the number by itself.
Triangular: add 1 + 2 + 3 + … up to the number.
Draw the dot pattern to check.
5 squared is 5 × 5 = 25, not 5 × 2 = 10.

p: A **factor** divides exactly into a number. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
A **prime number** has exactly **two** factors: 1 and itself (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, …). A **composite number** has more than two factors. 1 is neither.

lesson.t: Why primes have only two factors
p: A prime number can only be made as 1 × itself. A composite number has other factors because it can be made as a rectangle of dots.
Try dividing by 2, 3, 5, 7.
If any divides exactly, it is composite.
1 is neither prime nor composite.
9 is odd but composite: 9 = 3 × 3.
